items.s: You travel at the peak. In Europe the flu season usually starts between mid-November and mid-December and peaks in January or February.
items.do: Ask your GP whether a flu shot before you go is worthwhile for all five.

items.s: The worst outbreak there in decades: 2,597 cases and 29 deaths in 2025 with Prague the epicentre, and 1,078 more cases from January to May 2026. Czech officials say there is no need to cancel.
items.do: Wash hands before eating, and ask your GP about the hepatitis A vaccine.

items.where: The UK and most of Europe
items.s: Europe's surge is easing: 2,325 cases in the EU in the year to September 2026, and 66 in September. The UK lost its measles-free status in January. Most cases are in unvaccinated people.
items.do: Check all five of you have had two doses of the measles vaccine.

items.s: A large outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, with 11,197 confirmed cases by 12 November. A handful of patients have been flown to Europe for treatment. The EU's disease agency rates the risk to people in Europe as very low.
items.do: Nothing to do. It matters only if airports start health screening, and none was found on your route.
